claims.statement: DHS released the article on September 1, 2026.
The Science and Technology Directorate brought industry partners to the Progreso International Bridge to demonstrate facial biometric capabilities for Customs and Border Protection.
claims.quote: The Science and Technology Directorate (S&T) recently brought industry partners to the Progreso International Bridge border crossing in Texas to demonstrate facial biometric capabilities for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

claims.statement: The Progreso work was an operational assessment intended to support Customs and Border Protection planning.
claims.quote: When the industry partners arrived at the Progreso International Bridge in May, they began setting up for the operational assessment that would support CBP’s planning.

claims.statement: Some cameras were mounted at different heights to account for people of different statures.
claims.quote: Some cameras were mounted on poles at different heights to account for individuals of different statures.

claims.statement: The partners used AI and other technologies to model the capture zone, observe pedestrian movement, and assess whether facial images were suitable for biometric matching.
claims.quote: The partners leveraged artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies to perform tasks such as constructing a 3D digital environment of the image capture zone, observing pedestrian movement, and analyzing facial images to determine whether they were suitable for biometric matching in CBP’s Traveler Verification Service.

claims.statement: The technologies had to account for walking pace, hats, sunglasses, umbrellas, and other items people use or carry.
claims.quote: For the testing to be successful, the technologies had to account for human factors such as travelers’ walking pace, as well as hats, sunglasses, umbrellas and other items people use or carry.

claims.statement: Tests were conducted after dark using external lighting configurations.
claims.quote: Because ports of entry operate day and night, tests were also conducted after dark using external lighting configurations.

claims.statement: United States citizens were provided an opt-out lane if they declined the image-collection testing.
claims.quote: U.S. citizens were provided an opt-out lane if they chose not to participate in the image collection testing.

claims.statement: The Customs and Border Protection biometrics office said pedestrian image capture exceeded expectations in day and night conditions.
claims.quote: The image capture capabilities of pedestrians walking through the border exit area exceeded expectations in both day and night conditions.

claims.statement: The article publishes no numerical accuracy rate or image-retention period and announces no final selection for future deployment.
claims.quote: Each of these elements is equally important when supporting agencies like CBP, especially when assessing mission-critical technologies before they are selected for deployment.
claims.source: DHS Science and Technology Directorate, complete article
claims.evidence_scope: The validator re-read the complete article. It contains no numerical accuracy rate, image-retention period, or final future-deployment selection. The quotation anchors the source's pre-selection status; the absences are whole-document inferences.

rejected.claim: The assessment proved accurate facial matching.
rejected.reason: The article publishes no measured accuracy, false-match, or error rate.

rejected.claim: CBP made a final selection for ongoing deployment.
rejected.reason: The article describes an operational assessment and pre-selection planning.

rejected.claim: No technology was deployed operationally at the border.
rejected.reason: Technology was deployed for the assessment; only future selection remains unannounced.
No retention period, deletion schedule, or storage rule is published.

rejected.claim: AI made identity, immigration, or enforcement decisions.
rejected.reason: The source describes modeling, observation, and image-suitability analysis before matching.
The article describes the opt-out specifically for U.S. citizens.

evidence_policy: Every quoted passage was independently re-fetched from the complete DHS page. Typography is preserved from the live source; unsupported performance and deployment claims were dropped.
